title: James Webb Reveals a Strange Atmosphere on a Hellish Lava Planet
hook: A planet so hot its surface is an ocean of molten rock turns out to have a real atmosphere — built from gases venting straight out of the lava itself, JWST finds.
key_points: 55 Cancri e is a 'lava planet' hot enough to melt rock at its surface.
JWST data suggest it has a hydrogen-rich atmosphere.
That atmosphere appears shaped by gases escaping from the planet's molten interior.
There are signs volcanic outgassing may even create temporary clouds.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has taken a close look at 55 Cancri e, a so-called "lava planet" with temperatures high enough to melt rock right at its surface. The new data suggest this scorched world actually holds onto a real atmosphere — one that appears to be hydrogen-rich.
extra_html: Rather than a leftover from formation, the atmosphere seems to be shaped by gases escaping from the planet's molten interior — essentially the world venting its own guts into the sky. There are even signs that this volcanic outgassing could create temporary clouds, hinting that a planet extreme enough to have an ocean of lava can still host a dynamic, ever-changing atmosphere.

related.title: James Webb Finds Salt Clouds on a Mysterious Pink World
related.hook: GJ 504 b has puzzled astronomers for over a decade. James Webb finally read its atmosphere — and found the first direct evidence of salt clouds ever seen on a planet-like object.

related.title: An Alien World With Two Different Twilights
related.hook: On a scorching giant planet that never turns away from its star, the James Webb telescope found that dawn and dusk look nothing alike — winds smear the heat from one side to the other.

related.title: The First Atmosphere Found on a Rocky World in the Habitable Zone
related.hook: For the first time, astronomers have caught a rocky planet in its star's habitable zone holding onto an atmosphere — spotted by the helium slowly bleeding off into space.

related.title: A Giant Planet Was Hiding in the Dust Around Beta Pictoris
related.hook: A giant planet sat hidden for years inside one of astronomy's most-studied systems — Webb found it not by seeing it, but by sniffing out its atmosphere through a veil of dust.

flashcards.back_html: It's so hot that its surface is thought to be molten rock — an ocean of lava rather than solid ground.
